_doc: Revert-verify mutants for ticket 035da1eb (RFC 9821a379 AC5, core half): the SELECT envelope carries `variables` = the projection in declared order; `SELECT *` falls back to first-seen bound variables.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/exoql/evaluateWithExoEval.ts

VM1_binding_order._note: `variables` taken from the rows (binding order) — exactly what the RFC rules out. Also V8: in the alias-first GROUP BY query the row binds the group key ?s before the aggregate ?n, so binding order reads [s, n] against the declared [n, s].

VM2_alias_dropped._note: `(expr AS ?x)` projections skipped — an aggregate column disappears. Both alias axes: V4 (alias last) and V8 (alias first) lose the ?n column.

VM3_wildcard_as_empty_projection._note: `SELECT *` read as an empty projection — no columns at all. Also V7: it is a SELECT * axis too, and an empty projection lists no columns there.

VM4_no_store_drops_projection._note: The no-store envelope carries no columns.

VM5_alias_columns_appended_last._note: `(expr AS ?x)` columns appended after the plain variables — «in its place» is lost when the alias comes first (review 2026-10-24, form X2).

VM6_select_star_sorted._note: `SELECT *` columns sorted alphabetically instead of first-seen (review 2026-10-24, form X3).

VM7_select_star_first_row_only._note: `SELECT *` columns read from the first row only — a variable bound only in a later (OPTIONAL) row is lost (review 2026-10-24, form X4; the idiom §10(в) warns ticket 058bad52 against).
